text.p: German industrial and trading group Metallgesellschaft AG, which plunged into financial crisis three years ago, said on Friday it had matched its 1995/96 profit goal.

In an initial statement on its results for the business year ended September 30, MG said its pre-tax profit leaped 70 percent to over 290 million marks. The company had set a target of 300 million marks for its profit for the year.
"This means the company has managed to achieve the demanding target set out last year despite a deterioration in the economic conditions," MG said in a statement.
Turnover fell to 16 billion marks from the previous 17.6 billion as a result of the planned reduction in its trading activities. Staff levels were largely unchanged at around 23,300 employees.

Metallgesellschaft, which has been completely restructured since it ran into billions of marks of losses over risky oil deals in 1993, said it was now optimistic for the future and even raised the prospect of resuming dividend payments.
"For the current year, the group expects favourable developments to continue and to increase our earnings power, which will form a foundation for a renewed dividend payout," it said.
"The risk structure of Metallgesellschaft has been improved markedly by stopping our oil business," the statement added.
"With a further optimised group structure and a strategy which looks to the future the group believes it is optimally armed to compete internationally," it said.
MG said all parts of the company had reached their operating goals despite the economic weakness during the year.

MG Handel & Beteiligungen, its trading unit, had seen sales fall to seven billion marks from 8.7 billion, due to its increased concentration on its core business. MG said it had reported a clearly positive result for the year.

Engineering group Lurgi saw total output increase by 400 million marks to over 2.7 billion marks, while incoming orders fell to 2.2 billion marks from 2.5 billion. Its orders in hand edged slightly lower to six billion marks.
However it nonetheless managed to increase earnings.
Lentjes, which was merged with Lurgi at the start of the current business year, also saw a sharp gain in pretax profit.
MG Corp, the unit which was at the root of the spactacular losses on oil trading, had now been transformed into a smaller, profitable company trading in natural gas, it said.
